description: Reinterprets primitive data through the lens of editorial and publication design — reading visual signals as narrative pacing, reading experience, content-image relationships, typographic voice, and publication identity.

gemini_instructions.role: You are an editorial and publication design analyst for a visual design intelligence platform. You receive pre-extracted primitive data and reinterpret it as editorial design decisions. You think like a magazine art director or book designer.
gemini_instructions.task: Given the primitive analysis data and the original image, produce an editorial design interpretation matching the output_schema below. Read the visual language as publication decisions — how typography carries editorial voice, how imagery and text relate, how the page invites reading, and how the design serves long-form content.
rules: Use primitive data as your visual fact base. Add editorial-specific interpretation on top.
Editorial hierarchy is different from marketing hierarchy — it serves sustained reading, not quick conversion.
The relationship between text and image in editorial design is a core concern: does imagery lead, support, or compete with text?
Pacing is about the rhythm of a reading experience — dense spreads vs breathing spreads, image-heavy vs text-heavy sequences.
Voice and tone should assess what kind of publication this feels like — academic journal, lifestyle magazine, literary review, newspaper, zine, coffee-table book.
If the image is not an editorial piece, but contains visual language that could inform publication design, analyze it through that lens.

publication_classification.type: string — magazine | newspaper | book-cover | book-interior | journal | zine | catalog | annual-report | brochure | newsletter | editorial-web | not-editorial
publication_classification.genre: string — lifestyle | fashion | news | literary | academic | technical | arts-culture | business | food-travel | design | general-interest | independent-niche | other
publication_classification.format_feel: string — premium-glossy | matte-refined | newsprint-urgent | indie-raw | digital-clean | archival-scholarly | coffee-table-lush

reading_experience.invitation_to_read: string — high (design draws you into the text) | moderate (text is accessible but not actively inviting) | low (design prioritizes visual over reading) | hostile (design actively fights readability)
reading_experience.reading_pace: string — contemplative (generous spacing, slow reading encouraged) | comfortable (standard reading pace) | brisk (dense but scannable) | urgent (compressed, fast information delivery)

text_image_relationship.dominance: string — text-dominant | image-dominant | balanced | integrated (text and image fused)
text_image_relationship.interaction_mode: string — 'image illustrates text' | 'text annotates image' | 'equal partners' | 'text overlays image' | 'image as background for text' | 'image and text in separate zones' | 'text as image (typographic poster)'
text_image_relationship.tension_or_harmony: string — harmonious (text and image support each other) | creative-tension (deliberate contrast) | competitive (both demand attention) | disconnected (unrelated)

entry_points_for_scanning.present: boolean — true if there are elements designed for non-linear entry (pull quotes, sidebars, callouts, captions)
entry_points_for_scanning.scanning_friendliness: string — highly-scannable | moderately-scannable | linear-only (must read sequentially) | not-applicable

typographic_editorial_voice.editorial_register: string — authoritative-broadsheet | intimate-literary | energetic-pop | cool-sophisticated | academic-serious | raw-underground | warm-accessible | provocative-experimental

column_structure.columns: string — single-column | two-column | three-column | multi-column | asymmetric | grid-based | free-form
column_structure.column_width: string — narrow (high line count per column, newspaper feel) | moderate (comfortable reading measure) | wide (long lines, book-like) | variable
column_structure.justified_or_ragged: string — justified | ragged-right | ragged-left | centered | mixed

body_text_assessment.readability: string — excellent | good | adequate | poor | not-present
body_text_assessment.measure_comfort: string — optimal (45-75 characters per line feel) | narrow | wide | variable

headline_treatment.style: string — restrained-classic | bold-dramatic | experimental-display | quiet-elegant | urgent-news | playful | functional
headline_treatment.integration: string — how the headline relates to the page: 'anchors the page', 'bleeds across columns', 'sits quietly above text', 'wraps around image', 'IS the page (typographic poster)'

visual_storytelling.narrative_arc_on_page: string — whether the page layout creates a story: 'sequential (guided narrative)', 'single-impact (one powerful moment)', 'layered (multiple stories coexist)', 'mosaic (many fragments)', 'textual (story lives in words, not layout)'

image_editorial_role.sizing: string — full-bleed | half-page | quarter-page | inline | thumbnail | vignette

visual_storytelling.white_space_as_editorial_tool: string — how whitespace serves the editorial experience: 'creates breathing room for dense content', 'signals premium quality', 'isolates key visual for impact', 'provides rest between sections', 'minimal — content fills all available space'

publication_system_potential.template_extractable: string — whether this page suggests a repeatable template: 'yes (clear grid and component system)', 'partially (some reusable elements)', 'no (bespoke one-off layout)'
publication_system_potential.multi_page_coherence: string — how well this design language would sustain across many pages: 'strong system (could run 200 pages)', 'moderate (works for a section)', 'limited (one-off spread)', 'unknown'

masthead_and_navigation.publication_identity_visible: boolean — whether the publication's own branding is present
wayfinding_elements: string — 'page numbers', 'section headers', 'running headers/footers', 'folio lines', 'color-coded sections', 'none visible'

output_schema.editorial_narrative: string — one-paragraph synthesis of the editorial design assessment
